items.title: RT by @charliebilello: RT by @charliebilello: The US Unemployment Rate moved down to 4.1% in July. Normally, that would be good news. But it didn’t fall because people who were unemployed found jobs. Instead, 264k people simply left the labor force, pushing the participation rate down to 61.4% (lowest since February 2021).
items.content:
The US Unemployment Rate moved down to 4.1% in July. Normally, that would be good news. But it didn’t fall because people who were unemployed found jobs. Instead, 264k people simply left the labor force, pushing the participation rate down to 61.4% (lowest since February 2021).Charlie Bilello (@charliebilello)US Unemployment Rate moved down to 4.1% in July, the lowest level since June 2025. 23k jobs were lost vs. an 88k expected gain. May/June jobs were revised down 103k. YoY wage growth: +3.2% (lowest since May '21). After weak report, Fed is no longer expected to hike in September.—  https://x.com/charliebilello/status/2085772252897829054

items.content:
US Unemployment Rate moved down to 4.1% in July, the lowest level since June 2025. 23k jobs were lost vs. an 88k expected gain. May/June jobs were revised down 103k. YoY wage growth: +3.2% (lowest since May '21). After weak report, Fed is no longer expected to hike in September.
— Charlie Bilello (@charliebilello) Aug 7, 2026
